comment: Daily-refreshed feed of clinical breakthroughs, regulatory events, and guideline shifts. `audience` is 'general' (everyday-actionable, plain-English) or 'technical' (specialist-only). Public surfaces filter to general by default.

items.headline: Bone health: 600 METs-min/week of walking/jogging, plus falls risk assessment.
items.summary: Aim for 600 METs-min/week of brisk walking or jogging to boost bone density. Assess falls risk alongside exercise to prevent fractures.
items.why_it_matters: To protect your bones, do 600 METs-min/week of walking/jogging and talk to your doctor about fall prevention.

items.headline: FDA approves first mRNA flu vaccine, offering new protection against influenza
items.summary: The first mRNA-based flu vaccine received FDA approval. It uses technology proven in successful COVID-19 vaccines.
items.why_it_matters: Ask your doctor about the new mRNA flu vaccine when it becomes available this fall for better seasonal protection.

items.headline: FDA Approves New ADHD Medication
items.summary: The FDA approved a new medication for ADHD treatment. This provides an additional option for patients who may not respond to existing therapies.
items.why_it_matters: Patients with ADHD should discuss this new treatment option with their healthcare provider to determine if it's appropriate for their needs.

items.headline: New guideline adds blood test option for colorectal cancer screening
items.summary: The American Cancer Society now includes a blood test as a screening choice for colorectal cancer. This expands options beyond colonoscopy and stool tests.
items.why_it_matters: Ask your doctor if a blood test is a good screening option for you—it's less invasive than colonoscopy and may increase screening rates.

items.headline: Mechanical clot removal improves recovery for stroke patients with medium or distal artery blockages.
items.summary: Mechanical thrombectomy plus standard care improved recovery rates for stroke patients with medium or distal artery blockages. A higher percentage achieved functional independence at 90 days compared to standard care alone.
items.why_it_matters: If you or someone you know has a stroke with a medium or distal artery blockage, ask your doctor about mechanical thrombectomy as part of treatment.

items.headline: Thrombectomy for Stroke Clots in Smaller Arteries Improves Outcomes
items.summary: Adding mechanical thrombectomy to standard care improved functional recovery in stroke patients with medium or distal artery blockages. 60% of thrombectomy patients had good outcomes versus 40% with standard care alone.
items.why_it_matters: If you or someone you know has a stroke with a clot in a smaller artery, ask if mechanical thrombectomy is an option to improve recovery chances.

items.headline: Endovascular treatment for large stroke improves 1-year recovery compared to standard care.
items.summary: Patients with large stroke treated with endovascular thrombectomy had better one-year functional outcomes and survival rates than medical management alone. The benefit was significant for both measures.
items.why_it_matters: If you or a loved one has a large stroke, ask your doctor if endovascular treatment is appropriate for improved long-term recovery.

items.headline: New noninvasive scan finds clot source in stroke patients, improving treatment decisions
items.summary: Noninvasive imaging directly identifies blood clots in stroke patients. It frequently reveals the clot's origin, enabling more precise treatment planning.
items.why_it_matters: This test could lead to faster, more targeted stroke treatment in the future, improving recovery chances for patients.

items.headline: IV iron before heart surgery reduces blood transfusions and improves 90-day recovery
items.summary: A trial of 955 heart surgery patients found IV iron reduced blood transfusions. It also improved 90-day recovery rates, meaning more time alive and out of hospital.
items.why_it_matters: Ask your cardiac surgeon if IV iron before surgery could reduce your blood transfusion needs and speed up recovery.

items.headline: FDA approves home start for Alzheimer's antibody treatment
items.summary: The FDA approved a new subcutaneous starting dose for lecanemab, allowing patients to begin Alzheimer's treatment at home. This eliminates the need for an initial clinic visit.
items.why_it_matters: Alzheimer's patients can now start treatment at home, reducing travel burden for early therapy initiation.

items.headline: New algorithm safely rules out blood clots in cancer patients, avoiding CT scans
items.summary: A new diagnostic algorithm for blood clots in cancer patients was as safe and efficient as standard CT scans in a large trial. It reduced the need for CT scans, avoiding radiation and contrast exposure.
items.why_it_matters: Cancer patients may now avoid unnecessary CT scans for blood clot diagnosis, reducing radiation exposure and contrast use.

items.headline: FDA approves first oral drug to lower LDL cholesterol
items.summary: The FDA approved the first oral medication targeting LDL cholesterol reduction. Previously, such treatments required injections.
items.why_it_matters: Ask your doctor if this oral option could improve your cholesterol management plan.

items.headline: Pre-op iron reduces blood needs and improves recovery after heart surgery
items.summary: For heart surgery patients with anemia, a single 1000 mg iron dose cut blood transfusions from 68.2% to 61.1%. It also increased days alive and at home at 90 days.
items.why_it_matters: If you're having heart surgery with anemia, ask your doctor about pre-surgery iron to reduce blood transfusions and speed recovery.

items.headline: IV iron before heart surgery reduces need for blood transfusions by 7%
items.summary: IV iron before heart surgery reduced blood transfusion rates from 68.2% to 61.1%. This represents a 7.1% absolute risk reduction.
items.why_it_matters: If you're having heart surgery and have anemia, ask your doctor if IV iron could lower your risk of needing a blood transfusion.

items.headline: FDA approves gene therapy for children 2+ with sickle cell disease
items.summary: The FDA approved a gene therapy for children aged 2 and older with sickle cell disease who experience frequent pain crises or require regular blood transfusions. This treatment addresses the genetic cause of the condition.
items.why_it_matters: Parents of children with sickle cell disease should ask their doctors about this new treatment option for managing severe symptoms.

items.headline: Major heart groups agree on a single definition for heart failure
items.summary: Four leading heart organizations established a universal definition for heart failure. This standardizes diagnosis and treatment globally.
items.why_it_matters: Understand that heart failure is now defined consistently worldwide, improving diagnosis and care for millions of patients.

items.headline: New Guidelines Standardize Diagnosis and Treatment for Heart-Kidney-Metabolic Condition
items.summary: The guidelines provide unified methods for diagnosing and staging cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome. Updated treatment recommendations aim to improve care for millions affected by this interconnected condition.
items.why_it_matters: Ask your doctor how these new standards may impact your care plan for heart, kidney, and metabolic health.

items.headline: First Drug Approved to Lower Pancreatitis Risk in Severe High Triglycerides
items.summary: The FDA approved a new treatment for severe high triglycerides. It is the first drug shown to lower acute pancreatitis risk.
items.why_it_matters: If you have severe high triglycerides, ask your doctor about this treatment to help prevent pancreatitis.

items.headline: Blood thinner more effective than standard drug for migraines linked to heart hole
items.summary: A blood thinner reduced migraine frequency more than standard treatment in people with a heart hole (PFO). 78% of patients on the blood thinner had fewer migraines versus 62% on standard drug, a 16% absolute improvement.
items.why_it_matters: If you have migraines and a heart hole (PFO), ask your doctor if a blood thinner might be a better option than standard migraine medication.

items.headline: FDA approves first oral antibiotic for serious urinary tract infections
items.summary: The FDA approved the first oral carbapenem antibiotic for complicated urinary tract infections. This offers a convenient alternative to IV therapy for patients.
items.why_it_matters: Ask your doctor about this oral option for complicated UTIs to potentially avoid IV antibiotics and hospital visits.

items.headline: FDA approves first generic single-dose flu treatment, increasing affordability
items.summary: The FDA approved the first generic version of a single-dose influenza treatment. This will expand access and reduce costs for patients.
items.why_it_matters: Ask your doctor about this affordable flu treatment option for faster symptom relief during flu season.

items.headline: Web tool helps patients stay on antidepressants longer
items.summary:
Patients using a web-based decision-support tool were less likely to stop antidepressants early at 8 weeks.
This reduced discontinuation compared to standard care without the tool.
items.why_it_matters: Ask your doctor if a decision-support tool can help you stay on antidepressants longer for better depression management.

items.headline: Pregnant women using acetaminophen not linked to autism or ADHD in children
items.summary: A large study found no association between acetaminophen use during pregnancy and autism or ADHD in offspring. This confirms existing evidence on the safety of common pain relief during pregnancy.
items.why_it_matters: Pregnant people can safely use acetaminophen for pain relief as directed, without fearing autism or ADHD risks in children.

items.headline: FDA approves second over-the-counter naloxone nasal spray for opioid overdose
items.summary: The FDA approved a second over-the-counter naloxone nasal spray for opioid overdose emergencies. This increases access to life-saving treatment without requiring a prescription.
items.why_it_matters: Know naloxone is now available in two over-the-counter nasal spray forms, making it easier to keep at home for opioid overdose emergencies.

items.headline: First OTC glucose monitor approved for children with diabetes
items.summary: The FDA approved the first over-the-counter continuous glucose monitor for children. This device allows blood sugar monitoring without a prescription.
items.why_it_matters: Parents can now buy a glucose monitor for their child without a prescription, making diabetes management easier at home.

items.headline: AI-Powered Eye Scan Improves Diabetes Vision Screening Accuracy
items.summary: An AI-enhanced eye scan system improved detection of diabetic eye disease in a clinical trial. It showed better diagnostic accuracy and reduced unnecessary referrals compared to standard screening.
items.why_it_matters: If you have diabetes, ask your doctor about AI-enhanced eye screenings for early detection of vision-threatening complications.

items.headline: FDA approves first new sunscreen ingredient in 30 years
items.summary: The FDA approved bemotrizinol as the first new active sunscreen ingredient in over 30 years. This expands options for sun protection products available to consumers.
items.why_it_matters: Check sunscreen labels for bemotrizinol to access the first new active ingredient approved in over 30 years for sun protection.

items.headline: Ebola survivors may face long-term neurological issues, study finds
items.summary: A study found Ebola survivors often develop persistent neurological problems. These include memory loss and movement disorders lasting years.
items.why_it_matters: If you or someone you know survived Ebola, discuss long-term neurological monitoring with a healthcare provider.

items.headline: ACOG releases 2026 maternal immunization schedule, differing from CDC recommendations
items.summary: ACOG issued its first formal maternal vaccine schedule for 2026 that does not align with CDC guidelines. This marks a significant shift in obstetric care recommendations.
items.why_it_matters: Pregnant individuals should discuss vaccination plans with their OB/GYN, as ACOG's new schedule may change which vaccines are recommended during pregnancy.

items.headline: Post-surgery confusion linked to future memory problems in older adults
items.summary: Older adults who experience delirium after surgery are twice as likely to develop long-term cognitive decline. This risk remains even after accounting for other health conditions.
items.why_it_matters: If you or a loved one has surgery, ask your doctor about monitoring for postoperative confusion to address potential cognitive decline early.

items.headline: Removing fallopian tubes during routine surgery may lower ovarian cancer risk
items.summary: The European Society of Gynaecological Oncology recommends removing fallopian tubes during other gynecological surgeries to prevent ovarian cancer. This safe approach is now widely supported.
items.why_it_matters: Women having routine gynecological surgery should discuss removing fallopian tubes with their doctor to reduce ovarian cancer risk.

items.headline: FDA approves new drug for agitation in Alzheimer's dementia patients
items.summary: The FDA approved a new medication to treat agitation in Alzheimer's dementia. This provides a new treatment option for a common and distressing symptom.
items.why_it_matters: Families and caregivers of Alzheimer's patients now have a new treatment option for managing agitation, improving daily care and quality of life.

items.headline: WHO prequalifies first malaria treatment for infants under six months
items.summary: WHO prequalified a new malaria treatment designed for infants under six months. This is the first such treatment approved for this age group.
items.why_it_matters: Parents in malaria areas should seek immediate care for infants with fever, as a new infant-specific treatment is now available through health programs.

items.headline: Memory Changes May Predict Heart Events 8 Years Early
items.summary: Cognitive decline in older adults may precede cardiovascular events by up to 8 years. This could enable earlier detection of heart risks.
items.why_it_matters: Older adults noticing memory changes should discuss them with their doctor as they may signal future heart risks.

items.headline: Virtual neurology visits as effective as in-person for first-time patient evaluations
items.summary: Virtual neurology visits showed no significant difference in outcomes compared to in-person visits for initial patient evaluations. Patient satisfaction rates were comparable between both methods.
items.why_it_matters: Ask your doctor about virtual options for your first neurology appointment to reduce travel time without compromising care quality.

items.headline: Suicide Mortality Among Adolescents and Young Adults After Launch of a Suicide and Crisis Lifeline
items.summary: This study uses data from the National Vital Statistics System to examine quarterly suicide mortality among individuals aged 15 to 34 years.

items.headline: Datopotamab-deruxtecan extends overall survival in metastatic TNBC
items.summary: TROPION-Breast02 randomised 540 patients with previously-treated triple-negative breast cancer. Median OS 18.4 mo vs 14.0 mo with chemo (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.55-0.92).
items.why_it_matters: First TROP2-ADC to clear an OS benefit in TNBC. Likely registrational; expect filing inside 12 months.
